stem: HarborPay is decomposing a monolith into containerized services and wants to cut idle EC2 host spend while moving away from server patch cycles. (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Keep containers on fixed On-Demand EC2 hosts
Move each service to AWS Lambda zip functions
Run containers on AWS Fargate tasks
Scale microservices independently so only busy components grow
Purchase Standard Reserved Instances for every current EC2 node

rationale: Running containers on Fargate removes host management and ties billing to task-level resource usage. Scaling microservices independently reduces overprovisioning because only active components scale up. Fixed EC2 hosts keep patch and capacity-management burden. Lambda zip packaging is not a direct replacement for many containerized service patterns in this scenario. Reserving current EC2 nodes can lower unit price but does not remove patch cycles or idle host structure.
